newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures slightly higher.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures were slightly higher early, supported by firm Treasury bonds after early U.S. data.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures edged up to a new record high at 961.50, above the peak set Wednesday at 960.30. Traders said action was fairly quiet so far Thursday.

Treasury bonds were heartened by second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) and a first-quarter revision. GDP rose 2.2 percent in the second quarter and was revised downward to 4.9 percent from 5.9 percent in the first quarter.
Jobless claims fell to 277,000 in the latest week.
Claims in the previous week had been 299,000.
Traders said stock index futures continue to exhibit bullish technical momentum. Several traders put daily upside targets in the 966.00 handle.
One S&P 500 futures trader pegged intitial resistance at 961.50 and said the market should reach 966.50 by late morning.
He said a pullback to the old record high of 951.75 set Friday would be met by buyers.
"It could certainly sell down to there and still be buyable," the trader said.
September S&P 500s edged back from their record high after a second batch of U.S. data.

The Conference Board's U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose to 88.0 in June versus 81.0 in May. Chicago Purchasing Managers July index fell to 60.6 from 61.5 in June. The Chicago prices-paid index rose to 61.6 compared with June 53.7. Employment index at 51.0 in July versus 57.1 in June.
One firm pegged September S&P 500 fair value at 4.80 points premium to cash, buy programs at 6.00 points premium to cash or wider and sells at 3.80 points premium or narrower.

At 0909 CDT/1409 GMT, Sept S&P 500s were up 0.85 pts to 958.00, Nikkei rose 105.0 pts to 20,405.0, Midcap 400s rose 0.85 to 316.70, Russell rose 0.10 to 417.10, and NASDAQ fell 2.50 to 1106.75. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
